factors_doc: Habitat scoring model, not a prediction. Each block lists what the research says the animal is doing and the terrain it favours. Animals may not be there. cert (0 to 100) uses the CLAUDE.md scale; under 60 is a Tip, not a fact. Block cert is the certainty of the timing and activity claim. factors gives the certainty of each terrain factor; 0 means no data, the factor is neutral (aspect all 1, slope 0 to 90, sun any, water and road null, terrain any) and is listed in gaps. Tip lines carry 50 by convention. "My reading" lines are discounted from their source. Aspect weights are an encoding of written statements, not measurements: named aspects 1, next to a named aspect 0.7, the rest 0.4. slope_deg is [lo_ok, best_lo, best_hi, hi_ok] in degrees. Sourced percent grades are converted (degrees = atan(percent/100)). Where a source gives only best values, the shoulder (hi_ok = best_hi + 10, lo_ok = best_lo - 5) is a model choice. "Flat ground" = app flat class under 8 deg, shoulder to 15 deg. water_m is [best_max, ok_max] metres to water. "On the water" is encoded as [0, 60], one grid cell. road_m 500: hunters cluster within 0.5 km of open roads (Penn State 2004, 60% applied to BC). Elevation bands are general BC patterns from data/migration.json unless a month note names a local source for the owner's area. month_overrides hold full replacement values for the fields that change, plus the factors, gaps and note for that block.

mule-deer.name: Mule deer

1.note: Winter range: low south and west slopes, old Douglas fir. Kamloops: habitat rule below about 1,000 m (75%); a studied Kamloops winter range sat below about 760 m (80%, Willms 1976). Band from data/migration.json. Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

2.note: Winter range. Deep snow packs deer onto the warmest, steepest slopes. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

3.note: Still on winter range. First green grass shows on low south slopes late in the month. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

4.note: April: deer on low south facing grassy slopes; the BC account names the Dewdrop Range near Kamloops (90%). Migrants leave late April to May (85%). Band from data/migration.json. Area: Kamloops, Region 3.

5.note: Spring migration: most migrants go to summer range in April and May, often about 50 km, on the same route every year. Some deer stay low all year. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

6.note: Summer range: moister high country, openings, cutblocks and burns. Fawns born late May to June. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

7.note: Summer range high up. Resident deer stay on the lower slopes. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

8.note: Summer range in the high country until frost. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

9.note: Mostly still on summer range. Cold snaps and early snow up high start some moves. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

10.note: Heffley Creek before the first snow: bucks often mid slope about 900 to 1,500 m on open fir and burn edges (75%, Heffley Creek lesson). Snow up high moves them down (85%); general BC band 400 to 1,800 m (70%). Area: Heffley Creek, Region 3.

11.activity: rut on or near winter range
11.note: Most deer on or near winter range. Rut in November and early December. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

12.note: Winter range. In light snow years some deer stay higher until December. General BC pattern from data/migration.json (BEC zone ranges, not collar data). Area: Kamloops and Heffley Creek, Region 3.

tips.text: Snow, not the rut, pushes deer down to winter range. First snow up high: hunt mid slopes below the snow line.
No snow yet in October: bucks often mid slope, about 900 to 1,500 m, on open fir and burn edges near Heffley Creek.
Rut: find the does and stay out all day. Bucks follow them in daylight.
Morning sun warms the slope and your scent drifts uphill; in the evening it slides downhill. Approach from above in the morning.
Pressured deer use thicker cover and move more at night. Walk farther from roads than other hunters (most stay within 0.5 km).
Winter range is fragile. If deer are moving away from you, you are too close.
No approved ungulate winter range polygons around Kamloops and Heffley Creek; use the habitat rule: south and west slopes, grass, pine and fir below about 1,000 m.

tips.text: Most valley bottom land is private. Ask first, and check the private land layer before every sit.
Evening thermals drain cool air down to the river bottoms where white tails bed. Set up with that in mind.
Pressure turns white tails nocturnal and into thick cover. Midweek beats the weekend.
Late October: rubs then scrapes; bucks start moving in daylight.
Deep snow over about 40 cm pushes white tails onto winter range and packed trails.
No white tail season in Region 2; from Mission the nearest white tail hunting is Region 3 or 8.

tips.text: Willow, water and cover close together: that triangle is moose country.
Look for cutblocks 10 to 30 years old and burns 3 to 15 years old near wetlands.
November in Region 3: think food and cover, not calling. The main rut is over.
Evening air drains into low ground: keep your scent cone off the swamp.
Above about 14 deg C moose move less in the open. On warm days hunt the edges early and late.

Region 3 has no general elk season; Region 8 6 point bulls only. Check the Rule Book.

Young cutblocks (about 5 to 20 years) and burns (about 3 to 15 years) grow bear food; closed young forest grows little.

tips.text: Watch the flight line two evenings in a row before you plan a hunt.
The fields that hold geese are almost all private cultivated land: written permission first.
Light pressure near Heffley Creek: under 30 estimated goose hunters a year in MUs 3-27 and 3-28.
After a bright full moon, plan an afternoon hunt as well as a morning one.
Tranquille is a No Shooting area; Vaseux Lake is a sanctuary.
